summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for shortness of breath and hypoxia. Imaging revealed bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia, likely hospital-acquired or aspiration-related, though she was not found to be at aspiration risk. She was treated with a 7-day course of levofloxacin and supplemental oxygen, with improvement in oxygenation to 92% on room air by discharge. Her chronic pain, exacerbated by recent discontinuation of Lyrica and gabapentin, was addressed by restarting pregabalin at 75mg twice daily. A topical antifungal was used for urinary discomfort, which resolved. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable throughout. Medications were reconciled to reflect her actual home regimen. She was discharged home with services and follow-up planned.
